message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note**  
> * “EC2” is Amazon‑AWS terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.  
> * The RTX A6000 is available only in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and the **GPU quota** granted for your project.

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Set your project ID
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone us-central1-a \                     # pick a zone that supports A6000
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \             # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \           # optional: how to handle preemptible
    --restart-on-failure
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The GCP zone where the instance will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Selects the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Size & speed of the boot disk. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How to treat the instance during maintenance events. |

> 👉 **Tip**: If you want a *pre‑emptible* GPU VM, add `--preemptible`.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or Terraform), here’s a minimal JSON payload:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": { "items": [] },
  "tags": { "items": [] }
}
```

### Making the API call

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID. The `instance.json` file contains the JSON above.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| ✅ | Verify GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in your chosen zone |
| ✅ | Install the latest `gcloud` SDK |
| ✅ | Authenticate (`gcloud auth login` or `gcloud auth application-default login`) |
| ✅ | Choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 (check [GPU availability](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#available_zones)) |

Once the instance is created, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --zone us-central1-a
```

Happy computing! 🚀
